name: Departmental Test Paper IV: Kerala Treasury Code

lessons.title: Pensions (1)
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 272(a) Pension Payment Orders; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 272(aa) Pension Payment Orders; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 273(a) Register of Pension Payment Orders; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 294(a) Lapse of pensions; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 295
points: Payment of pensions can be made only on pension payment orders issued by an Accountant General, except military pensions and cases the Government orders otherwise.
The disburser's half stays in the treasury of payment, and the other half is given to the pensioner when he first appears for payment.
The register of Pension Payment Orders is kept in Form T.R. 80.
Service pensions and family pensions from the State consolidated fund fall due from the first day of the month to which the pension relates.
Pension is payable for the whole month in which the pensioner dies, whatever the date of death.
Family pension begins from the first day of the month following the month of the pensioner's death.
A pension payable in India that remains undrawn for more than one year ceases to be payable.
Arrears cease to be payable if not claimed within one year of the pensioner's death.
remember: Pension payment orders are issued only by an Accountant General (except military pensions).
Register of PPOs: Form T.R. 80. PPO has two halves: disburser's half and pensioner's half.
Pension for the whole month of death; family pension from the 1st of the next month. Undrawn over one year: pension ceases.

questions.q: Who issues Pension Payment Orders?
questions.why: Pensions are paid only on PPOs issued by an Accountant-General (KTC Rule 272(aa)).

questions.q: In which form does the Treasury Officer keep the register of Pension Payment Orders?
questions.why: The register of PPOs issued on his treasury is in Form T.R. 80 (KTC Rule 273(a)).

questions.q: A pensioner dies in the middle of a month. For how much of that month is pension payable?
options: Up to the date of death only
Up to the end of the week of death
questions.why: Pension is payable for the whole month of death, whatever the date (KTC Rule 298).

questions.q: From when does family pension commence after the pensioner's death?
options: First day of the month of death
First day of the month following the month of death
questions.why: Family pension starts from the first day of the month following the death (KTC Rule 298).

questions.q: After how long does an undrawn pension payable in India cease to be payable?
questions.why: Pension undrawn for more than one year ceases to be payable (KTC Rule 294(a)).

lessons.title: Pensions (2)
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 271 Definitions, political pension; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 271 Definitions, service pension; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 280(a) Life certificate; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 286(vii) Pension by postal money order; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule
points: In the month of December every year, or pension for January and later months is held up until it is received.
Once in three years, by personal appearance or a certificate of continued existence.
A fee of Rs 5 is levied before a duplicate Pension Payment Order is issued.
A pension that is not a service pension, granted on political grounds, compassionate grounds, distinguished or meritorious services, or surrender of rights.
A pension payable in consideration of past employment under the Government of India or any State, including gratuity or family pension so payable.
A political pension not drawn for six years ceases to be payable without the previous sanction of the Accountant General.
remember: Annual life certificate: produced in December; otherwise January and later pensions are held up.
Money order pensioner: existence verified once in three years. Duplicate PPO fee: Rs 5.
Political pension undrawn for six years ceases without Accountant General sanction.

questions.q: In which month must a pensioner who does not appear produce the annual life certificate?
questions.why: The certificate is produced every December, failing which January pension is held up (KTC Rule 280(a)).

questions.q: How often must the disbursing officer satisfy himself of the existence of a money order pensioner?
questions.why: Continued existence is checked once in three years (KTC Rule 286(vii)).

questions.q: What fee is levied before a duplicate Pension Payment Order is issued?
questions.why: A fee of Rs 5 is levied on the pensioner (KTC Rule 293(a)).

questions.q: A political pension not drawn for how many years ceases without the Accountant General's sanction?
questions.why: A political pension undrawn for six years ceases without prior AG sanction (KTC Rule 297(a)).

questions.q: Which pension is paid in consideration of past employment under the Government of India or a State?
questions.why: This is the definition of service pension in KTC Rule 271.

lessons.title: Bills
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 163(q) Form of bills, endorsement; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 17 Special instructions to Treasury Officers; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 18 Exceptions; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 188(viii) Contingent bills endorsed to private party; Kerala Treasury Co
points: A bill or cheque can be endorsed only once, in favour of the specific party to be paid, with some exceptions for bankers and agents.
Three months after the date of endorsement or at the end of the financial year, whichever is earlier.
The drawing officer issues an advice in Form T.R. 106 to the Treasury Officer giving full particulars of the bill.
Payment is made in the district in which the claim arises, unless Government orders otherwise.
For the first of any series of payments in a district, except for a newly appointed person, the claim must have a last pay certificate.
Not unless the certificate is first surrendered.
No. Honorarium to a gazetted officer by the Kerala Public Service Commission is an exception to the Accountant General intimation rule.
It should not be paid if presented three months after the date of enfacement or authorisation.
remember: A bill or cheque is endorsed only once. Contingent bill endorsement lapses after three months or at year end, whichever is earlier.
Advice for endorsed contingent bill: Form T.R. 106. AG enfaced bill not paid after three months.
Last Pay Certificate needed for first payment in a district (not for newly appointed); no pay drawn after LPC issued unless surrendered.

questions.q: How many times can a bill or cheque normally be endorsed?
questions.why: It can be endorsed only once in favour of the party to be paid (KTC Rule 163(q)).

questions.q: When does an endorsement on a contingent bill lapse?
options: At the end of the financial year only
Three months after endorsement or at end of the financial year, whichever is earlier
questions.why: Rule 210(i): lapses at three months or year end, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: In which form is the advice sent to the Treasury Officer for a contingent bill endorsed to a private party?
questions.why: The drawing officer issues the advice in Form T.R. 106 (KTC Rule 188(viii)).

questions.q: Where is a payment, in general, made for a claim?
options: In the district in which the claim arises
In any district the claimant chooses
questions.why: Payment is made in the district where the claim arises unless Government orders otherwise (KTC Rule 17).

questions.q: A bill enfaced by the Accountant General presented after how long should not be paid?
questions.why: It should not be paid if presented three months after enfacement (KTC Rule 210).

lessons.title: Verification Of Balance
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 42 Verification by the Director; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 46(1) Responsibilities of the Treasury Officer; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 47 Responsibilities of the Treasury Officer; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 52(a) Verification on change of Treasury O
points: At least once in three months, without prior intimation to any staff member, and a certificate goes to the Accountant General and Finance Department.
He must verify the district treasury balance in person on the first of each month and sign the account.
In no case more than two consecutive months.
Cash (coins and notes) is verified once every month. Stamps, opium, ganja and other valuables once every six months.
At least twice a month.
Once a month for non-banking sub treasuries, and once in three months for banking sub treasuries, without prior notice.
He must verify the cash balance as per Rule 144 and report the result to the Accountant General with a certificate in Form T.R.1.
remember: Director of Treasuries verifies each district treasury cash balance at least once in three months, without notice.
DTO verifies balance in person on the 1st of each month; never more than two consecutive months skipped. Cash monthly; stamps, opium, ganja six-monthly.
Sub Treasury Officer: at least twice a month. DTO verifies banking sub treasuries once in three months. Relieving officer reports in Form T.R.1.

questions.q: How often must the Director of Treasuries verify each district treasury's cash balance?
options: At least once in three months
questions.why: Verification is without prior intimation to staff (KTC Rule 42).

questions.q: On which day must the Treasury Officer verify the district treasury balance in person?
options: The last day of each month
questions.why: KTC Rule 47: in person on the first of each month.

questions.q: How many consecutive months may pass without the Treasury Officer verifying the monthly closing balance?
questions.why: In no case more than two consecutive months (KTC Rule 47).

questions.q: How often are stamps, opium and ganja verified by the Treasury Officer?
questions.why: Cash monthly; stamps, opium, ganja every six months (KTC Rule 46(1)).

questions.q: How often must the Sub Treasury Officer verify the sub treasury cash balance?
options: At least once in three months
questions.why: KTC Rule 60: at least twice a month.

lessons.title: Currency Chest
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 135 Note 1, Treasury balance and currency chest balance; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 152 Note 2, Currency chest book; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 152(i) Currency chest instructions; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 152(iii) Currency chest instructions; Kera
points: The contents are the property of the Reserve Bank, but Government is responsible to the Reserve Bank for them.
Treasury balance is the Government's cash balance used for its payments and receipts. A separate currency chest is also ordinarily kept in the treasury.
Every transaction must be in even hundreds of rupees.
A currency chest book in Form T.R. 37 is kept in the chest and signed at every transaction by the officials in joint charge.
It is retained for three complete financial years after it ceases to be in use.
A serially numbered slip in Form T.R. 38, signed by the two officers in charge, goes to the Currency Officer, Madras, after closing.
At the close of each month, by the officer who verifies the treasury balance.
remember: Currency chest contents belong to the Reserve Bank; Government is responsible for them.
Every transaction in even hundreds of rupees. Currency chest book: Form T.R. 37, kept three complete financial years after use.
Daily slip: Form T.R. 38 to Currency Officer, Madras. Balance verified at close of each month.

questions.q: Whose property are the contents of the currency chest?
questions.why: They belong to the Reserve Bank, but Government is responsible for them (KTC Rule 135 Note 1).

questions.q: Every currency chest transaction should be in what value?
questions.why: KTC Rule 152(i).

questions.q: Which form is the currency chest book?
questions.why: The book in Form T.R. 37 is signed at every transaction by officials in joint charge (KTC Rule 152(iii)).

questions.q: How long is a currency chest book retained after it ceases to be in use?
questions.why: KTC Rule 152 Note 2.

questions.q: To whom is the daily currency chest slip in Form T.R. 38 sent?
questions.why: It is sent when the treasury closes for the day (KTC Rule 152(v)).

lessons.title: Strong Room
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(a) Treasury strong room; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(c) Treasury strong room; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(d) Treasury strong room; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(f) Treasury strong room
points: A Public Works officer not lower than an Executive Engineer must certify the place as secure and fit for use as a strong room.
Every strong room is inspected yearly by the Executive Engineer or his deputed officer, and the Treasury Officer obtains a safety certificate.
The Executive Engineer is responsible for the building and fixtures. The Treasury Officer is responsible for chests and furniture not part of the building.
Strong room doors and windows stay permanently closed and locked, except while coin or valuables are moved in or out.
remember: A PWD officer not below Executive Engineer must certify a strong room secure.
Strong room inspected annually; Treasury Officer obtains a safety certificate.
Executive Engineer responsible for building and fixtures; Treasury Officer for chests and furniture. Doors and windows kept closed and locked.

questions.q: Who must certify a place as secure and fit for a strong room?
options: A PWD officer not lower than an Executive Engineer
questions.why: KTC Rule 136(a).

questions.q: How often must every strong room be inspected?
questions.why: Inspected annually, and the Treasury Officer obtains a safety certificate (KTC Rule 136(c)).

questions.q: Who is responsible for the security of the strong room building and its fixtures?
questions.why: KTC Rule 136(d); the Treasury Officer is responsible for chests and furniture.

questions.q: When may the doors and windows of the strong room be open?
options: Only while moving coin or valuables in or out
Whenever the Treasury Officer is present
questions.why: They stay permanently closed and locked otherwise (KTC Rule 136(f)).

lessons.title: Anamath
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 114 Anamaths; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 118 Anamaths
points: The treasurer keeps the Anamath Balance Register in Form T.R. 19.
The Treasury Officer verifies the anamath balance every evening.
As a rule, money may be kept in a strong room only if paid into the Government account and part of the treasury balance.
No. Money must not be kept in anamath for want of information on the nature of the credit or pending confirmation of a sale.
remember: Anamath Balance Register: Form T.R. 19, kept by the treasurer.
Treasury Officer verifies the anamath balance every evening.
No money in strong room unless paid into Government account. No anamath for want of information or pending confirmation of sale.

questions.q: In which form is the Anamath Balance Register kept?
questions.why: The treasurer maintains it (KTC Rule 114).

questions.q: When does the Treasury Officer verify the anamath balance?
questions.why: KTC Rule 118.

questions.q: As a general rule, what money may be kept in a treasury strong room?
options: Any money received by the treasury
Only money paid into the Government account and forming part of the treasury balance
questions.why: KTC Rule 114.

questions.q: Can money sent for payment into the Government account be kept in anamath for want of information on its nature?
options: Yes, with the Treasury Officer's order
Yes, until the Accountant General replies
questions.why: Money must not be so kept, nor pending confirmation of a sale (KTC Rule 118).

lessons.title: Cheques
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 245(b) Cheques; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 250 Lost cheques; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 251 Cancelled cheques
points: A cheque remains current only for three months from the date of issue.
He must at once report to the Treasury Officer and ask him to stop payment of the cheque.
Only after receiving the Treasury Officer's signed certificate that the cheque has not been paid, and after cancelling the original cheque.
He must cancel any cheque that has remained unpaid for twelve months from the date of issue.
remember: A cheque remains current only three months from issue.
Lost cheque: report at once to the Treasury Officer to stop payment. New cheque only after his signed certificate and cancelling the original.
Drawing officer cancels a cheque unpaid for twelve months.

questions.q: For how long does a cheque remain current?
options: Three months from the date of issue
questions.why: KTC Rule 245(b).

questions.q: On learning a cheque is lost, what must the drawing officer do?
options: Report at once to the Treasury Officer and request stoppage of payment
Report to the Accountant General only
questions.why: KTC Rule 250.

questions.q: When may a new cheque be issued in place of a lost one?
options: After the Treasury Officer's signed certificate and cancelling the original
questions.why: KTC Rule 250.

questions.q: After how long must the drawing officer cancel an unpaid cheque?
options: Twelve months from date of issue
questions.why: KTC Rule 251.

lessons.title: Deposits
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 205(a) Repayment of revenue deposits; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 207 Repayment of revenue deposits and criminal court's deposits; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 210(q) Repayment of revenue deposits
points: No. An earnest money deposit shall never be repaid in part.
A revenue deposit is repaid only on the order of the court or authority which ordered its acceptance.
No payment is made after the close of the financial year of issue or three months from the date of issue, whichever is earlier.
remember: Earnest money deposit is never repaid in part.
Revenue deposit repaid only on order of the court or authority that ordered its acceptance.
Repayment order for revenue or criminal court deposit: not paid after year end or three months, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: Can an earnest money deposit be repaid in part?
questions.why: KTC Rule 210(q).

questions.q: On whose order is a revenue deposit repaid?
options: The court or authority that ordered its acceptance
questions.why: KTC Rule 205(a).

questions.q: Within what time must a repayment order for a revenue or criminal court deposit be paid?
options: Before year end or three months from issue, whichever is earlier
questions.why: KTC Rule 207.

lessons.title: Double Lock Keys
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 135(a) Custody and verification of the treasury balance
points: The Treasury Officer holds the key of one padlock and the Chief Treasurer holds the key of the other.
Each officer puts his key in a leather bag, sealed by a subordinate with the official seal and the Treasury Officer's private seal.
remember: District strong room has two padlocks: Treasury Officer holds one key, Chief Treasurer the other.
At final closing, each officer puts his key in a leather bag sealed by a subordinate.
Both the official seal and the Treasury Officer's private seal are affixed to each bag.

questions.q: Who holds the keys of the two padlocks of a district treasury strong room?
options: Treasury Officer and Sub Treasury Officer
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(a).

questions.q: In what is each key placed when the strong room is finally closed for the day?
questions.why: The bag is sealed by a subordinate in presence of both officers (KTC Rule 135(a)).

questions.q: Which seals are affixed to each key bag?
options: Only the Treasury Officer's private seal
The official seal and the Treasury Officer's private seal
The Chief Treasurer's seal and the official seal
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(a).

lessons.title: Padlocks And Keys
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 137(a) Treasury padlocks and keys; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 137(c) Treasury padlocks and keys
points: A register of all padlocks and keys is kept in Form T.R. 29 in the district treasury strong room.
The Treasury Officer must at once report to the Director of Treasuries and send the padlock for lever alteration and new keys.
remember: Register of padlocks and keys: Form T.R. 29, kept in the district treasury strong room.
It covers the district treasury and its sub treasuries.
Lost key: report at once to the Director of Treasuries and send padlock for lever alteration and new keys.

questions.q: In which form is the register of padlocks and keys kept?
questions.why: KTC Rule 137(a).

questions.q: Where is the register of padlocks and keys kept?
options: In the district treasury strong room
questions.why: KTC Rule 137(a).

questions.q: If a treasury padlock key is lost, whom must the Treasury Officer report to at once?
questions.why: He also sends the padlock for lever alteration and new keys (KTC Rule 137(c)).

lessons.title: Double Lock Receptacles
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 139(d) Receipt of moneys into and issue of moneys from double locks; Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 139(h) Receipt of moneys into and issue of moneys from double locks
points: Never more than one double lock receptacle may be kept unlocked at a time, and it must not stay open longer than necessary.
He must prove the balance whenever money moves between double locks and single lock, or between double locks and the currency chest.
remember: Never more than one double lock receptacle unlocked at a time.
It must not stay open longer than necessary.
Balance is proved when money moves between double locks and single lock, or double locks and the currency chest.

questions.q: How many double lock receptacles may be kept unlocked at one time?
questions.why: KTC Rule 139(d).

questions.q: When must the Treasury Officer prove the balance?
options: Only when a key is lost
When money moves between double locks and single lock or currency chest
questions.why: KTC Rule 139(h).

questions.q: How long may a double lock receptacle be kept open?
options: Until the end of the day
questions.why: KTC Rule 139(d).

lessons.title: Treasurer'S Custody
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 135(b) Custody and verification of the treasury balance
points: The amount held by the Treasurer should not ordinarily exceed Rs 5,000, and a request for more must be carefully scrutinised.
remember: Cash held by the Treasurer in separate custody should not ordinarily exceed Rs 5,000.
Requests for a larger sum must be carefully scrutinised by the Treasury Officer.

questions.q: What is the usual limit of cash the Treasurer may hold in separate custody?
questions.why: The amount should not ordinarily exceed Rs 5,000 (KTC Rule 135(b)).

questions.q: Who sees that the Treasurer's separate custody amount does not exceed the limit?
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(b).

questions.q: How should a Treasurer's request for a larger sum be treated?
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(b).

lessons.title: Treasury Balance
lessons.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 135(a) Custody and verification of the treasury balance
points: The bulk of the balance, called the main store or double lock balance, is kept in the strong room under double locks.
remember: The bulk of the treasury cash balance is the main store or double lock balance.
It is kept in the treasury strong room under double locks.

questions.q: What is the bulk of the treasury cash balance generally known as?
options: Main store or double lock balance
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(a).

questions.q: Where is the main store of the treasury cash balance kept?
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(a).

questions.q: Under what kind of locks is the main store kept?
questions.why: KTC Rule 135(a).
